title: Punnett squares
assumptions: Equal allele segregation, independent assortment for two loci, random fertilization, and equal viability. Two-locus linkage, epistasis, penetrance and selection are not included. Repeated gametes intentionally retain equal-probability cells. X-linked outcomes assume equal probability of X- and Y-bearing sperm.

title: Pedigree analysis
assumptions: A fixed three-generation family; unrelated founders; one locus; complete penetrance; no new mutation, phenocopy or ascertainment correction. Sex symbols represent the XX/XY inheritance model. Founder genotypes have equal prior probability within each sex/model; offspring are weighted by Mendelian transmission. Conditional probabilities depend on these teaching priors and are not clinical risk estimates. Compatibility is checked by enumerating complete family assignments, not by visual heuristics.

title: Population growth
assumptions: Continuous time, closed population, constant r and K, no age structure or time delay. Analytic solutions avoid numerical integration error. For r > 0, logistic growth is greatest at N = K/2; a population starting above K declines toward K. Negative r is permitted, but the logistic model above K can then diverge and is limited to its finite solution domain.

title: Predator–prey dynamics
assumptions: Homogeneous populations, constant rates, mass-action predation, and no immigration or age structure. The extension replaces αx with αx(1−x/K); it retains linear predation and is not a saturating functional-response model. Fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration uses 12,000 steps. These are model outputs, not field counts. Impossible numerical trajectories stop with an error.

title: Gel electrophoresis
assumptions: A schematic for linear double-stranded DNA from 100 to 10,000 bp. The log-size migration relation is an approximation with an adjustable plotting span, not a calibrated gel prediction. Gel concentration, voltage, buffer and DNA conformation are not simulated. Circular uncut plasmids do not obey this linear-DNA model. Fragments closer than the resolution threshold are merged into one displayed band; brightness scales with represented DNA mass assuming equal molecule counts, not measured loading.

title: Micropipette readings
assumptions: Conventional three-digit teaching displays: P20 = tens/ones/tenths µL; P200 = hundreds/tens/ones µL; P1000 = thousands/hundreds/tens µL. Hardware displays and ranges vary: use your instrument manual. Readings are nominal settings, not delivery guarantees. Statistics describe entered measurements; they do not establish calibration acceptance.

title: pH & acid–base models
assumptions: Ideal dilute aqueous solutions at 25 °C: concentration approximates activity. Strong-acid calculation includes water autoionization. Weak-acid calculation solves charge balance, mass balance and Kₐ together, including water autoionization. The buffer uses the Henderson–Hasselbalch approximation with equilibrium concentrations approximated by supplied concentrations; it is not a titration or buffer-capacity simulation. pH paper colors are illustrative, not a calibration chart. The displayed meter is rounded to 0.01 pH; no instrument uncertainty is inferred.

title: Water & hydrogen bonding
assumptions: Schematic molecular arrangements, not a molecular-dynamics simulation. Temperature changes a qualitative motion indicator, not a calculated bond lifetime. Ice geometry is illustrative rather than crystallographically exact.

title: Element & atom accounting
assumptions: Formula parsing counts atoms; it does not infer molecular structure, bond energy, or reaction feasibility.

title: Polymer assembly & hydrolysis
assumptions: Each displayed link represents one condensation/hydrolysis event. This is an accounting model, not a universal cellular synthesis mechanism; nucleic-acid synthesis, for example, uses activated nucleotides.

title: Carbohydrate structure
assumptions: Stylized glucose residues, not atomic structures. Branch frequency is schematic; starch also includes branched amylopectin. No rate of digestion is predicted.

title: Lipids & membrane packing
assumptions: Schematic packing only. No physical fluidity value is calculated. Cholesterol restrains movement at higher temperatures and disrupts tight packing at lower temperatures; behavior depends on membrane composition.

title: DNA & RNA strand studio
assumptions: Sequence complementarity only; secondary structure, melting temperature and biochemical kinetics are not predicted.

title: Protein interactions & disruption
assumptions: Qualitative examples. Actual effects depend on residues and conditions; unfolding is not calculated. Heat or pH do not automatically break peptide bonds. Disulfide reduction changes covalent crosslinks.

title: Organelle disruption & trafficking
assumptions: A canonical secreted protein is assumed to have an ER-targeting signal. Free-ribosome products and organelle-targeted proteins can follow different routes. Disruption outcomes are schematic, not calculated protein concentrations.

title: Cell size & diffusion distance
assumptions: Ideal geometries without membrane folds. For cylinders, size means radius; both end caps are included. Surface-area-to-volume ratio does not independently determine a maximum viable cell size.

title: Diffusion & transport saturation
assumptions: Compartments remain well mixed and volumes fixed. Carrier mode uses an illustrative reversible saturable flux P(CA−CB)/(1+(CA+CB)/Km). Coefficients are entered model parameters, not inferred membrane permeabilities. No membrane potential or active transport is included.

title: Selective membrane permeability
assumptions: Qualitative permeability comparison. A matching protein represents an appropriate channel/carrier, not any arbitrary membrane protein. This tool predicts a route, not a numerical transport rate.

title: Water potential
assumptions: Ideal solutions, fixed temperature, water-permeable membrane, and no gravity or matric contribution. Output predicts initial direction, not flow rate or final cell volume. Temperature uses °C + 273.15. MPa = bar / 10. Pressure can counteract solute effects.

title: Tonicity & cell volume
assumptions: External reservoir is effectively infinite. Internal nonpenetrating solute amount is conserved. Penetrating solute equilibrates and contributes no sustained osmotic gradient in this simplified model. Animal-cell volume prediction ignores rupture. Plant-cell walls and pressure prevent using the animal-volume formula as a plant-cell prediction.

title: Osmosis data investigation
assumptions: Fits an ordinary least-squares line to entered percent changes. The zero crossing is an estimate only when a linear approximation is justified and measurements bracket zero. Assumes an open solution with sucrose (i=1) when calculating its solute potential. Tissue pressure is not inferred.

title: Ion gradients & active transport
assumptions: Stoichiometric pump accounting; ion concentrations do not change from the displayed cycle count. Nernst potential is a college extension for a K⁺-selective membrane and is not the full resting potential.

title: Compartmentalized reactions
assumptions: Illustrative reaction with a competitive inhibitor. Boundary condition selects whether inhibitor reaches enzyme; transport rates, volume changes and substrate delivery are not simulated.

title: Endosymbiosis evidence
assumptions: Evidence explorer, not a historical simulation. Individual observations differ in strength and are not assigned numerical proof scores. Shared features alone do not uniquely establish a full evolutionary sequence.

title: Enzyme investigation studio
assumptions: Michaelis–Menten steady-state model with irreversible product formation and no product inhibition. Enzyme is entered in µM, so rate is µM/min; progress converts to mM/min. Temperature uses a stated illustrative Q10=2 rise with a logistic high-temperature activity loss; pH uses a Gaussian response. These response functions are not measured kinetics or irreversible time-dependent denaturation. Km, kcat and inhibition mechanisms are college extensions.

title: Activation energy & catalysis
assumptions: Illustrative reaction-coordinate paths, not measured molecular energy surfaces. Both barriers must exceed reactant and product energy.

title: ATP coupling & feedback
assumptions: Energetic bookkeeping assumes reactions are mechanistically coupled. ATP free-energy change is entered for the conditions and is not a universal constant. Feedback is a qualitative pathway example.

title: Photosynthesis & electron flow
assumptions: Stoichiometric upper-bound teaching model. Uses an assumed 3 ATP per 8 photons for bookkeeping; actual ATP production depends on coupling and cyclic electron flow. Does not simulate carbon-fixation kinetics, photorespiration, or absorbed-light efficiency. Blocking ATP synthase can also impede electron flow; that feedback is not dynamically modeled.

title: Photosynthesis investigation
assumptions: Empirical saturating response with constant respiration. Irradiance is in relative units. Leaf-disk view maps accumulated net gas to float fraction using an explicit illustrative threshold distribution; it is not a calibrated prediction for real disks. Pigment composition, CO₂ limitation and photoinhibition are outside this model.

title: Respiration & chemiosmosis
assumptions: Qualitative steady-state disruption examples with adjustable ATP yield for accounting. A blocked ATP synthase eventually slows ETC via backpressure; an uncoupler separates electron flow from ATP production. No detailed carrier kinetics or fixed ATP-per-glucose total is asserted.

title: Fermentation & NAD⁺ regeneration
assumptions: Ideal stoichiometric accounting for the listed pathways. Does not predict real fermentation rate, cell growth or gas pressure.

title: Respirometer data investigation
assumptions: Entered data are measurements supplied by the user. Assumes CO₂ absorption, comparable temperature/pressure effects and calibrated displacement volumes. Uses endpoint average rate, not a mechanistic respiration prediction.

title: Communication & receptor binding
assumptions: Equilibrium binding with no cooperativity or ligand depletion. Occupancy is not the same as downstream response. Mismatch is modeled as no specific binding. Communication route is schematic and does not calculate transport time.

title: Signal transduction & amplification
assumptions: Discrete illustrative cascade with a 10,000-unit response ceiling. Amplification units are arbitrary and not fitted biochemical rate constants. Constitutive relay activation bypasses the receptor but does not bypass an effector block.

title: Feedback & homeostasis
assumptions: Deviation magnitude is nonnegative. The positive example is bounded amplification, not a model of every biological positive-feedback system. The positive ceiling is a saturation limit, not a homeostatic set point. No delay or oscillatory controller is included.

title: Cell cycle, DNA content & mitosis
assumptions: Diploid cell with conventional mitosis. Anaphase counts separated sister chromatids as chromosomes within the still-undivided cell. C indicates DNA content relative to one unreplicated haploid genome.

title: Mitotic-index investigation
assumptions: Duration inference assumes a steady-state asynchronous population with comparable survival and sampling. A synchronized population or changing proliferation can invalidate the estimate.

title: Cell-cycle checkpoints
assumptions: Rule-based schematic of selected checkpoints. Real regulation involves multiple pathways; a single defect does not guarantee cancer or unrestricted proliferation.

title: Meiosis & nondisjunction
assumptions: One nondisjunction event in one chromosome pair is assumed. Crossing over is not included in the combination count. Meiosis II error occurs in one of the two cells. Gamete types are equally represented in this schematic.

title: Linkage & recombination
assumptions: Testcross to ab/ab with equal viability and no segregation distortion. Recombination fraction cannot exceed 0.5. Recombination percentage approximates map distance for short intervals; multiple crossovers cause underestimation for longer intervals.

title: Multiple alleles & epistasis
assumptions: ABO uses the standard simplified single-locus model; rare exceptions are excluded. Epistasis example defines aa as masking the B locus, giving 9:3:4 under independent assortment and equal viability.

title: Polygenic trait distributions
assumptions: Two heterozygous parents at every independent locus; additive equal effects; no epistasis or dominance. Environment adds independent normally distributed variation. These assumptions do not describe every quantitative trait.

title: Environment & phenotype
assumptions: Illustrative linear reaction norms over a limited environment range. Negative trait values may be meaningful only for traits defined as deviations; choose appropriate baselines. No heritability is estimated.

title: DNA replication fork
assumptions: One fork schematic; sequence complementarity is exact. Okazaki fragment lengths, origin spacing, enzyme movement and error rates are not simulated.

title: Transcription & RNA processing
assumptions: RNA conversion and selected position removal are exact sequence operations. The removed interval is designated as an intron/excluded exon for this teaching example; real splice-site recognition is not inferred. No promoter or transcription start site is predicted.

title: Translation & reading frames
assumptions: Standard genetic code, explicit frame offset, and no automatic initiation-site selection. Output uses amino-acid one-letter codes and stops at the first in-frame stop. An incomplete terminal codon is ignored.

title: Gene regulation: operons
assumptions: lac uses lactose as shorthand for the allolactose inducer; low glucose enables CAP-mediated activation. trp shows repressor/corepressor logic and omits attenuation. Outputs are qualitative levels, not transcript concentrations.

title: Cell specialization & expression
assumptions: A schematic expression program with housekeeping expression retained and cell-type-specific expression controlled by one regulator. Real cell identity involves many interacting regulators and chromatin states. Numerical output is normalized model expression, not measured RNA abundance.

title: Mutation consequences
assumptions: This tool analyzes a specified coding frame beginning at the first base. It does not predict protein function, organismal fitness or regulatory effects. Standard genetic code; one-base indels shift the frame.

title: PCR amplification
assumptions: Constant efficiency with no plateau or reagent depletion. Counts are expected copies, not necessarily integers. Target length is entered, not inferred from primers. This view does not model nonspecific binding or primer design.

title: Restriction digest & fragments
assumptions: Exact recognition-site scan for the listed enzymes, including circular wraparound sites. Assumes complete digestion and ignores methylation, star activity and enzyme-accessibility effects. Cut positions refer to the displayed strand. Uncut circular DNA does not migrate like equal-size linear DNA.

title: Transformation & selection
assumptions: Expected transformant count = cells × probability. Assumes all cells viable, marker expression complete before plating, and susceptible cells unable to grow on antibiotic. No colony-count calibration, competence protocol or resistance dosage is modeled.

title: Selection & resistance evolution
assumptions: Infinite diploid population, random mating, constant viability selection, no drift, mutation or migration. Resistance scenario is a conceptual allele-fitness example, not a bacterial clinical or treatment model.

title: Selection on trait distributions
assumptions: One generation of selection on a normally distributed standardized trait. Fitness functions are explicit teaching examples: exp(sx), exp(−sx²), or 1+sx². No inheritance response or universal ecological optimum is inferred.

title: Artificial selection response
assumptions: College extension: quantitative-genetic expectation under additive inheritance and stable environment. Selection differential is fixed relative to the changing population mean each generation. Heritability is population/environment-specific and does not measure how genetically determined an individual trait is.

title: Genetic drift, founders & bottlenecks
assumptions: Neutral Wright–Fisher model with discrete nonoverlapping generations, no migration, selection or mutation. Founder/bottleneck changes the initial sampled allele pool once; subsequent generations use the entered N. Seed fixes reproducibility.

title: Gene flow between populations
assumptions: Equal-sized infinite populations with symmetric replacement migration, no selection or drift. Frequency changes are calculated simultaneously each generation.

title: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
assumptions: Diploid biallelic locus. Frequency comparison is descriptive and does not identify a cause of departure. Allele frequency is estimated from the same sample; a formal HWE chi-square test therefore has one degree of freedom and can be unreliable with small expected counts.

title: Evolutionary sequence evidence
assumptions: Assumes a valid alignment of equal-length homologous sequences. p-distance is uncorrected for multiple substitutions and is not a phylogenetic reconstruction method. Similarity alone does not establish orthology or ancestral direction.

title: Phylogenetic-tree studio
assumptions: Four-taxon rooted cladograms with no branch-length time or genetic-distance scale. Internal nodes represent inferred ancestors; none of the tip species is labeled as another tip’s ancestor.

title: Isolation & divergence
assumptions: Infinite two-population allele model: A favored in one population and a favored in the other with additive genotype fitness. Frequency divergence does not itself establish reproductive isolation or a new species.

title: Origins-of-life evidence
assumptions: Curated reasoning activity, not a reconstruction of the origin of life. Experimental possibility does not prove that an exact laboratory condition or sequence occurred on early Earth.

title: Environmental responses: taxis & kinesis
assumptions: One-dimensional bounded arena; cue increases left to right. Reflecting boundaries prevent escape. Taxis adds a positive directional bias; kinesis changes random step size. Output is an illustrative behavioral model, not fitted animal behavior.

title: Trophic energy & productivity
assumptions: Steady-state energy-accounting example. Constant transfer efficiency is an entered assumption, not a universal 10% rule. Producer respiration cannot exceed GPP in this nonnegative-NPP view. Biomass and numbers are not calculated directly from energy.

title: Carbon, nitrogen & phosphorus pools
assumptions: Closed three-pool accounting model. Uptake applies to the chosen available chemical pool; nitrogen fixation, nitrification and phosphorus weathering are not resolved separately. Energy is not represented by this conserved pool.

title: Population accounting & demography
assumptions: Fixed counts per interval rather than per-capita rates. Negative projected population is truncated at zero; births and departures then no longer follow fixed biological assumptions, so interpretation should stop at extinction. Age structure is not modeled.

title: Population sampling investigation
assumptions: Mark–recapture assumes a closed population, retained marks, thorough mixing and equal capture probability. Quadrat inference assumes representative independent sampling and known habitat area. Outputs are point estimates; no confidence interval is asserted.

title: Density dependence & disturbance
assumptions: Piecewise logistic dynamics with instantaneous disturbance. The event changes population and K independently; the chosen cause is not inferred. Recovery is impossible from exact zero without immigration.

title: Competition & coexistence
assumptions: Lotka–Volterra competition model with fixed intrinsic rates 0.2 time⁻¹. Species are homogeneous; resource identity and spatial refuges are not explicit. Outcome depends on coefficients and starting state.

title: Food webs & trophic cascades
assumptions: Illustrative three-level chain: dP=.5P(1−P/300)−.02PH; dH=.005PH−.2H−.03HC; dC=.006HC−.1C. Parameters are examples, not a prediction for a named ecosystem. Removal is complete at t=0; no recolonization.

title: Mutualism & parasitism
assumptions: Illustrative bounded model, not a universal mutualism/parasitism law. Each species has baseline logistic growth .2N(1−N/100); interaction is ±sN(other/(50+other)). A is the host in parasitism.

title: Biodiversity: richness & evenness
assumptions: Entered sample counts are treated as representative. Shannon and Simpson indices are college extensions and depend on sampling effort. High diversity does not automatically prove ecosystem resilience.

title: Nutrient enrichment & oxygen
assumptions: Illustrative three-state eutrophication model with nutrient recycling, biomass loss, and reaeration toward 8 mg/L. Rates are not calibrated to a lake. Oxygen demand is proportional to biomass, with saturation at low oxygen to prevent negative O₂. Does not model temperature, stratification or species-specific tolerance.

title: Graphing & descriptive statistics
assumptions: Replicates must represent independent experimental units. Error bars are not automatic significance tests. No normality check or confidence interval is inferred. Rows are ordered by X for plotting; choose a numerical X only when appropriate.

title: Chi-square goodness of fit
assumptions: Goodness-of-fit test with an externally specified expected ratio unless fitted parameters are entered. Independence and adequate expected counts are required. Uses 0.05 critical values for df 1–10. Fail to reject does not prove the null hypothesis. Small counts trigger a validity warning.

title: Experimental design & simulated replicates
assumptions: Synthetic independent replicates generated with Box–Muller normal sampling. True means and SD are model inputs, not estimated causal facts. No hypothesis test or causal conclusion is automatically asserted. Seed supports reproducibility.

title: Pigment absorption & action spectra
assumptions: Illustrative Gaussian absorption bands centered near common pigment peaks, not measured spectra. Composite action curve is a normalized weighted sum and excludes energy-transfer efficiency and leaf optical effects.

title: PCR primer binding & target span
assumptions: Exact-match teaching model without mismatch tolerance, melting temperature, secondary structure or off-target genome search. Primers must be at least 4 bases here; real primers are typically longer. Multiple inward-facing pairs are reported rather than arbitrarily choosing one.

title: Circadian cues & entrainment
assumptions: Illustrative oscillator with discrete daily phase correction toward the nearest environmental cycle. It does not model a molecular clock or a biological phase-response curve. The waveform is arbitrary relative activity.

title: Invasion & resource competition
assumptions: Both species have K=100; resident r=.2 and introduced r=.25 time⁻¹. Coefficients are hypothetical; introduced species are not universally competitively superior. The model excludes enemies, facilitation and spatial heterogeneity.

title: Habitat loss & patch connectivity
assumptions: Levins-style college extension with homogeneous patches and mass-action colonization. Initial occupancy cannot exceed remaining habitat. Habitat loss is represented by h; connectivity is represented by c. Occupancy is not population abundance.

title: Functional diversity & response
assumptions: Illustrative functional-response accounting: equal initial contributions; diverse sensitivities range from 0.2 to 1, while identical sensitivity is 0.6. Remaining contribution = max(0,1−severity×sensitivity). This selected scenario does not establish a universal diversity–resilience law or simulate recovery.
